**Test Image Observations:**
- Small, curved/bent young shoot or inflorescence (C/U shape)
- Pale yellow-green base color
- Multiple brown/dark necrotic spots scattered along its length
- Delicate, slender structure — isolated on white background

**Reference Image Comparison:**

- **Anthracnose**: Leaves with irregular brown necrotic patches, yellowing, tip/margin damage — brown lesion pattern on leaf tissue
- **Bacterial_Canker**: Elongated leaves with brown marginal necrosis running along edges
- **Cutting_Weevil**: Bare stems with triangular stubs where leaves were cut — no leaves remaining
- **Die_Back**: Fully desiccated brown elongated leaves — complete tissue death
- **Gall_Midge**: Green mango leaves with distinct small raised dark bumps/galls dotting the surface
- **Powdery_Mildew**: White powdery circular patches on leaf surface
- **Sooty_Mould**: Dark gray/black sooty coating mixed across green leaf surface

**Reasoning:**
The test image shows a curved young shoot/inflorescence with scattered brown necrotic spots. This does not match Cutting_Weevil (no cutting pattern), Die_Back (not fully desiccated), Bacterial_Canker (no marginal necrosis), Powdery_Mildew (no white powder), or Sooty_Mould (no sooty coating). The raised bump galls seen in Gall_Midge references don't match. The scattered brown irregular lesions on this young shoot tissue most closely match **Anthracnose**, which commonly attacks young mango shoots and inflorescences causing brown necrotic spotting and distortion.
